data.name: TUNNEL DIVERS
data.detailed_description:
Welcome to your new line of work, pilot.

TUNNEL DIVERS is an online free to play action game featuring futuristic space fighters that are specialized in destroying hordes of robots in enclosed spaces. With plenty of ships and weapons, claustrophobia won't be the most dangerous thing in the tunnels.


TUNNEL DIVERS is free to play and has no pay-to-win attached. Play online with your friends and against other pilots without feeling disadvantaged because you didn't pay for any DLC. The only one who should be paying are the suits from TAC-CORP!


TUNNEL DIVERS is a lightning fast twin stick shooter, you need to keep your ship on the move while combating hordes of robots or enemy players. Only those with the best reflexes and aim can come out as the top pilot.

Play cooperatively with your friends in Gauntlet, run the flag in Capture the Flag or just slaughter your enemies in Dogfight mode. More game modes on the way.


Looking for a challenge? Experience a fully designed single player campaign, with 20 unique hand-made missions and 4 different boss fights. With full ship loadout customization, you can spec your ship to speedrun each mission, or to barely scrap by passing the extra challenging superior performance review.


Vaporize your enemies with powerful weaponry, from long range laser guns to destructive miniature nuclear bombs.

Completely customize how your ship of choice is loaded out with weapons and special modules that can give you an edge in a fight. Earn money by completing matches and unlock more and more equipment.


Whether it's a single player mission made by a friend or a competitive multiplayer map made by a stranger, Workshop implementation allows you join matches with player made maps, even if you haven't downloaded the files yourself yet.


Enjoy the musical talent of Gergely Kovács, who composed a full soundtrack for the game.

data.short_description: Dive, destroy and escape. TUNNEL DIVERS is a F2P high octane twin stick shooter, where you pilot a close quarters based spaceship that excels in claustrophobic areas. Play online with or against other pilots, create your own levels in the level editor, and wage war against the rogue AI, Watch Dog.

reviews.review:
TUNNEL DIVERS is a fast little space shooter that caught me off guard with how much it actually puts into such a simple idea. I am flying a small futuristic ship through tight tunnels while fighting robots, and the enclosed spaces make everything feel much more frantic than a normal space shooter. I have to keep moving because there is not much room to hide, and the game can quickly turn into a mess of enemies, bullets and explosions. I like that the whole game is built around this close quarters idea because it gives the shooting a clear identity instead of just being another space game.

The movement is probably the strongest part for me. The ship feels quick and I have to constantly think about where I am going because the tunnels leave me with limited space to work with. The single player campaign has 20 handmade missions and four boss fights, which gives me a decent amount of actual content to work through. I also like that I can change my ship loadout with different weapons and modules, so I can adjust how I want to approach the tougher missions. There are weapons ranging from laser guns to miniature nuclear bombs, and the ability to change my equipment gives the combat more variety than I expected.

I also like the level editor because it gives the game more value outside of the main campaign. I can create my own levels and use the Workshop to play through maps made with the editor. That fits the game really well because the basic mechanics are simple enough to understand, but there is still room to make more complicated arenas once I know what I am doing. The different multiplayer modes also give me more ways to use the shooting system, including cooperative Gauntlet, Capture the Flag and Dogfight. I do not need all of these modes to enjoy the game, but having them there makes the package feel much bigger.

The biggest problem for me is that the close quarters design can sometimes become more frustrating than exciting. I like the pressure of having limited room, but when several enemies are attacking at once it can become difficult to tell exactly what I should be avoiding. The fast movement also means I can get myself into trouble very quickly. I think the difficulty is part of the appeal, but there are moments where I feel like I am fighting the cramped environment as much as I am fighting the actual enemies. It works better for me when I am already comfortable with the controls and know how much space I need to leave myself.

The presentation is simple, but I think it suits the game. The futuristic ships, enclosed tunnels and pixel style give it a nice old school arcade feeling, while the soundtrack helps keep the action moving. I do not think the game needs a huge story or detailed environments because the shooting is clearly supposed to be the main attraction. I also appreciate that the free to play version is not built around pay to win equipment. There is paid VIP content, but the main game gives me the campaign, multiplayer, ship equipment and level editor without requiring me to buy an advantage.

Overall, TUNNEL DIVERS is a fun little shooter that does a good job with its claustrophobic space combat. I like the quick movement, weapon choices, handmade campaign, bosses and level editor, and I think the free price makes the amount of content even easier to appreciate. The difficulty can sometimes become messy and the limited space is not always as enjoyable as it is intended to be, but the game has enough personality to stand out. For me, it works best when I want something quick, difficult and focused on pure shooting rather than a huge progression system.

Rating: 7/10
